title: When Must You Use a Qualified Medical Interpreter?
summary: Learn when healthcare organizations need a qualified medical interpreter, how qualification differs from certification, when bilingual staff can interpret, and what Section 1557 requires.
body_markdown:
###


A qualified interpreter can interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially in both directions and can handle the specialized vocabulary needed for the communication.


###


Not exactly. Certification is a formal credential. Qualification refers to whether the person has the competence needed for the interpreter role under the applicable standard.


###


When interpretation is needed to provide meaningful access, the healthcare organization must use language assistance that meets the applicable quality requirements for the communication.


###


Yes, if they have been assessed for the interpreter role and have the language and interpreting skills needed for the communication. Bilingual ability by itself is not enough.


###


No. Section 1557 does not prescribe one universal interpretation modality for every encounter. The focus is meaningful access and appropriate language assistance for the patient and communication at issue.
